source_title: Vaught's conjecture for theories of discretely ordered structures
title: Simple types cut out initial parts that are type-definable, discretely ordered and closed under minima

standard_prerequisites.name: The definition of a simple type over A, witnessed by a subset C of the definable closure and a linear order (D,<)
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Set up in the definitions preceding the counted statement; used throughout the counted proof
standard_prerequisites.use: Fixes the data the four clauses quantify over and the meaning of C-type used in each step.

standard_prerequisites.name: The uniqueness of the simple type p extending the C-type condition
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Used inside the counted proof at line 155
standard_prerequisites.use: Lets a point whose type is finitely satisfied in C but not algebraic be identified with p, giving the initial-part claim.

core_obligations: Clause (a): show that P(M) = C union p(M) is an initial part of (D,<) by taking b < a with a in p(M) and proving that every formula in the type of b is realised in C, so that the type of b is either algebraic or equal to p; then exhibit the type-definition P(x) = exists y (theta(y) and x < y) over p (proof lines 151-156).

Clause (b): with c_0 = min C, use the formula expressing that [c_0,x] is discretely ordered, note that it holds on C and hence lies in p, and take D_0 to be the union of the intervals [c_0,a] for a satisfying it, which is A-definable, discretely ordered and contains P(M) (proof line 159).

Clause (c): for a relatively definable nonempty D_1 inside P(M), choose a in p(M) meeting it, use the formula expressing that [c_0,x] meet theta(M,y) has a minimum, transfer it from C to a by the C-type property, and conclude that D_1 has a minimum (proof lines 162-168).

Clause (d): compare two witnesses with orders agreeing on C; assuming they disagree on P(M) produces, for each a in p(M), a minimum b of the set of points below a in one order and above it in the other, which by clause (a) lies in p(M) and yields a smaller such point, a contradiction (proof lines 171).
proof_roadmap: Prove the initial-part and definability statements by transferring formulas from C to p (proof lines 151-156).
Use the same transfer for the discrete-order and minimum clauses, and finish the uniqueness clause by a minimality contradiction (proof lines 159-171).
difficulty_reason: The lemma describes what a simple type over a set A does to the witness order attached to it: the set P(M) = C union p(M) is an initial part that is type-definable over A, it sits inside an A-definable discretely ordered initial part, every relatively definable nonempty subset of it has a minimum, and two witnesses whose orders agree on C agree on all of P(M) (statement lines 138-148). The proof transfers formulas between C and p in each clause: the C-type property is what moves a formula satisfied on C up to the realisation a, and it is applied once for the initial-part claim, once for the discrete order, once for the minimum, while the last clause is a minimality argument inside P(M) (proof lines 151-171). The step that carries the content is the transfer in clause (c), since it converts a statement about the finite interval [c_0,c] into a statement about the possibly infinite interval below a; the other clauses reuse the same mechanism. H2.
